@graph.name: Nagi
@graph.description: I believe you can make great food with everyday ingredients even if you’re short on time and cost conscious. You just need to cook clever and get creative!

@graph.name: Slow Cooked Rosemary Lamb Ragu
@graph.description: Recipe video above. Lamb Ragù is a wonderful way to use lamb shoulder for a generous, comforting meal that feels far more luxurious than the cost suggests. The lamb is slow cooked in a rich red wine tomato sauce until it's fall apart tender, gently shredded then tossed back in the sauce. The rosemary flavour in this is beautiful - please try to use fresh rather than dried!For pasta shapes, pappardelle is the classic, but anything with good meat-catching abilities works so have fun! Try capunti paesani (pictured - little canoe shapes), mafaldine, paccheri, fusilloni or rigatoni. Just avoid tiny pasta like risoni or fine strands like angel hair.Note: I've written the directions around 1 packet of pasta but you'll have ragu leftover to make another 1 - 2 servings, depending on how generous you are with the sauce.
recipeIngredient: 1.25 kg / 2.5 lb  boneless lamb shoulder (, excess fat trimmed and cut into 3 equal pieces (Note 1))
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((half for table salt, +50% for flakes))
2  celery sticks (, grated using a box grater (discard stringy bits))
1  large carrot (, peeled, grated with box grater)
1 tbsp rosemary (, finely chopped (substitute 2 tsp dried))
2  bay leaves (, preferably fresh else dried)
2  beef stock cubes (, crumbled (I use OXO, crumbles perfectly))
3/4 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((half for table salt, +50% for flakes))
500g / 1 lb  pappardelle, mafaldine, rigatoni, capunti paesani ( or other shapes with shredded meat catching abilities! (Note 2))
1 tbsp cooking salt / kosher salt (, for pasta cooking water)

itemListElement.text: Brown lamb, cook soffrito slowly, cook off tomato paste, deglaze and reduce wine. Slow cook lamb in sauce 2 hrs, remove, shred, simmer 30 min to reduce. Toss with cooked pasta!
itemListElement.name: Brown lamb, cook soffrito slowly, cook off tomato paste, deglaze and reduce wine. Slow cook lamb in sauce 2 hrs, remove, shred, simmer 30 min to reduce. Toss with cooked pasta!

itemListElement.text: Brown lamb - Sprinkle lamb with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. Brown 2 pieces of the lamb until deep golden on both sides, about 2 - 3 minutes per side. Remove into a bowl and repeat with the 3rd piece, adding more oil if needed, then remove.
itemListElement.name: Brown lamb - Sprinkle lamb with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. Brown 2 pieces of the lamb until deep golden on both sides, about 2 - 3 minutes per side. Remove into a bowl and repeat with the 3rd piece, adding more oil if needed, then remove.

itemListElement.text: Soffrito - Lower heat to medium, cool the pot a bit if it's very hot and scrape out any loose black bits (pepper, lamb bits) but leave any tasty lamb fat in there. Add a bit of oil if your pot is looking a bit dry. Then add the onion, celery, carrot, garlic and rosemary. Cook slowly for 7 - 8 minutes until softened but don't let them colour. Don't rush this step, it's key for good ragu flavour.
itemListElement.name: Soffrito - Lower heat to medium, cool the pot a bit if it's very hot and scrape out any loose black bits (pepper, lamb bits) but leave any tasty lamb fat in there. Add a bit of oil if your pot is looking a bit dry. Then add the onion, celery, carrot, garlic and rosemary. Cook slowly for 7 - 8 minutes until softened but don't let them colour. Don't rush this step, it's key for good ragu flavour.

itemListElement.text: Deglaze and reduce wine - Turn heat up to high and add the tomato paste. Stir for 1 1/2 minutes to cook out the sourness and deepen the colour from red to brown. Then add the wine and simmer rapidly, scraping the base of the pot, until reduced by half.
itemListElement.name: Deglaze and reduce wine - Turn heat up to high and add the tomato paste. Stir for 1 1/2 minutes to cook out the sourness and deepen the colour from red to brown. Then add the wine and simmer rapidly, scraping the base of the pot, until reduced by half.

itemListElement.text: Slow cook - Add tomato, stock, 3 rosemary sprigs, bay leaves, crumbled stock cubes, salt and pepper. Mix, add lamb (and any juices in the bowl) and let it come to a simmer. Then put the lid on and reduce the heat to low or medium low so it's simmering very gently. Slow cook for 2 hours or until the lamb is tender enough to shred. (Note 3 for other cook methods)
itemListElement.name: Slow cook - Add tomato, stock, 3 rosemary sprigs, bay leaves, crumbled stock cubes, salt and pepper. Mix, add lamb (and any juices in the bowl) and let it come to a simmer. Then put the lid on and reduce the heat to low or medium low so it's simmering very gently. Slow cook for 2 hours or until the lamb is tender enough to shred. (Note 3 for other cook methods)

itemListElement.text: Shred - Remove lamb and shred using two forks. Cut excessively long strands using scissors. (Keep the pot on stove on medium heat without the lid while you do this).
itemListElement.name: Shred - Remove lamb and shred using two forks. Cut excessively long strands using scissors. (Keep the pot on stove on medium heat without the lid while you do this).

itemListElement.text: Reduce sauce - Remove and discard rosemary and bay leaves. Return lamb into sauce and add the remaining 2 rosemary sprigs. Toss, then simmer on medium low for 30 minutes with the lid off, stirring every now and then, until the sauce has reduced and is thickened. Taste, and add more salt if needed. Cover and keep warm while you cook the pasta.
itemListElement.name: Reduce sauce - Remove and discard rosemary and bay leaves. Return lamb into sauce and add the remaining 2 rosemary sprigs. Toss, then simmer on medium low for 30 minutes with the lid off, stirring every now and then, until the sauce has reduced and is thickened. Taste, and add more salt if needed. Cover and keep warm while you cook the pasta.

itemListElement.text: Cook pasta - Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the salt. Add the pasta and cook per the packet directions minus 1 minute (so it's a little underdone, it will finish cooking in the ragu).
itemListElement.name: Cook pasta - Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the salt. Add the pasta and cook per the packet directions minus 1 minute (so it's a little underdone, it will finish cooking in the ragu).

itemListElement.text: Reserve water - Just before draining, scoop out a mugful of the cloudy pasta water. Drain pasta.
itemListElement.name: Reserve water - Just before draining, scoop out a mugful of the cloudy pasta water. Drain pasta.

itemListElement.text: Toss - Return pasta into the pasta cooking pot with 6 - 7 cups (1.2 - 1.4kg) of the warm ragu (start with 6, add another cup if you want). Set the pot over medium high heat. If your ragu was very thick rather than saucy (it thickens the longer it is sitting around), add 1/4 to 1/3 cup pasta cooking water. Then toss with spatulas until the meat is tangled through the pasta and all the pasta is stained red, there should be no sauce pooled in the bottom of the pot. If at anytime the pasta gets too stiff and sticky, just add more pasta cooking water.

itemListElement.text: Serve - Divide between warmed pasta bowls or pour into a large serving bowl and let everyone help themselves with parmesan on the side! Add a side of Garlic Bread and a fresh Balsamic Rocket Salad on the side and finish with a beautiful Tiramisu. :)

review.reviewBody: OMG. what a dish! Each year I ask my husband what he would like for his birthday dinner but this year, I didn’t ask and decided to prepare this for him (honestly because I wanted it!) and we both loved it.  Flavors were delicious. Excellent and easy to prepare early in the day and simply reheat just before serving. Nagi, I simply love your recipes. I am breaking out of my rut of ‘same old same old’ and working my way through your site. Thanks and love from the USA.

Seriously the best Ragù recipe I have ever made. The depth of flavour was outstanding. I did have to adjust the cooking time as I only had bite sized pieces of lamb shoulder left over from another recipe so there was  no shredding. I’m so impressed that I’m about to make it again. Thanks Nagi….. you never disappoint 😘❤️

Hi Nagi we often use your recipes thank you! I made this lamb ragu tonight. We had a boned shoulder but it still worked and I cooked it in the oven for about an hour longer. I replaced the celery with fennel stems as I grow fennel and I used veg stock instead of chicken. Very delicious and went well with our home made pasta and veggie garden salad. You do a wonderful job at providing easy to follow recipes. 🙏🙏❤️

Absolutely delicious! 😋 One of the perks of working from home is being able to have something bubbling away in the kitchen while you're working. And let me tell you, the smell wafting through the house all afternoon was enough to make me hungry hours before dinner!

Mine took a little longer than the suggested 2½ hours, more like 3 hours and 15 minutes, but who cares when the end result is this delicious? The lamb was melt-in-your-mouth tender and that sauce... YUM!

I've even stashed a few portions in the freezer for those days when I can't be bothered cooking. Nothing like having a delicious home-cooked meal ready to go when you're feeling lazy! 😂

Another absolute winner, Nagi! Keep these recipes coming. You're making takeaway look very ordinary! ❤️

Well, I had plans this weekend but saw this recipe...  Could not find lamb shoulder and ended up getting cubed lamb stew from Whole Foods.  It came out beautifully!  Made the whole recipe and froze it in batches.  So good!!!
